text: Who is credited with coining the term 'Artificial Intelligence' in 1956?
explanation: John McCarthy coined the term 'Artificial Intelligence' in 1956 and is regarded as the father of AI.

text: Which component of AI enables computers to identify faces; objects; and scenes in photographs?
explanation: Computer Vision allows AI systems to interpret and understand visual information such as images and video.

text: An expert system that helps diagnose car engine faults has three core components. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
explanation: Expert systems consist of a knowledge base; inference engine; user interface; rules base; and explanation system. A spreadsheet module is not a component.

text: What does Natural Language Understanding (NLU) refer to in AI?
optionB: Enabling machines to understand spoken or written language
explanation: NLU refers to the AI capability that enables machines to understand and interpret human language input.

text: A doctor uses an AI system to suggest possible diagnoses by matching patient symptoms against a database of medical knowledge. This is best described as:
explanation: Expert systems use a knowledge base and inference engine to suggest solutions or diagnoses; mimicking expert human reasoning.

text: Which of the following correctly describes a 'smart city' feature enabled by AI?
optionA: A city where all residents own a smartphone
optionB: A city that uses data-driven technology to manage transport; energy; and public services
optionC: A city with fibre-optic internet only
optionD: A city where all government forms are digital
explanation: Smart cities use AI and data analytics to manage infrastructure such as traffic; energy grids; waste; and water systems more efficiently.

text: Extended reality (XR) is an emerging technology referenced in the Cambridge ICT syllabus. Which TWO technologies does XR encompass?
explanation: Extended reality includes virtual reality (VR) — a fully immersive digital environment — and augmented reality (AR) — digital overlays on the real world.

text: Which of the following is an example of system software?
explanation: Device drivers are system software that allow the operating system to communicate with hardware devices. The others listed are applications software.

text: A microcontroller embedded in a washing machine to control its wash cycles is best described as:
explanation: Embedded computers are microprocessors built into other devices to control specific functions; such as in washing machines; cars; and industrial equipment.

text: Which of the following correctly describes analogue data?
optionA: Data stored as a series of 0s and 1s
optionB: Data that varies continuously with no discrete steps
optionC: Data organised into tables and records
optionD: Data compressed into a smaller file
explanation: Analogue data is continuous and can take any value within a range; unlike digital data which is discrete (0s and 1s).

text: A student uses a head-mounted display to explore an ancient Roman city without leaving the classroom. Which technology is this?
explanation: Virtual reality (VR) creates a fully immersive simulated environment; experienced through head-mounted displays (HMDs).

text: What is the main advantage of wearable technology such as a fitness tracker?
optionA: It replaces the need for a desktop computer
optionB: It monitors health data continuously without requiring a separate device
optionC: It can install any operating system
explanation: Wearable technology such as fitness trackers continuously monitor data like heart rate and steps taken; providing health insights on the go.

text: Prolonged use of ICT equipment can cause Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI). Which part of the body is MOST commonly affected?
explanation: RSI is caused by repetitive movements such as typing or using a mouse; and commonly affects the wrist and hand/arm area.

text: A tablet computer that uses Wi-Fi and Bluetooth and is primarily used for entertainment and education is an example of:
explanation: Mobile computers — including tablets; smartphones; and laptops — are portable and designed for use while on the move.

text: In a relational database; which field uniquely identifies each record in a table?
explanation: A primary key is a field (or combination of fields) that uniquely identifies every record in a database table.

text: A database table stores student ages as whole numbers only. Which data type is most appropriate for this field?
explanation: Integer (a numeric sub-type) stores whole numbers without decimal places; making it appropriate for ages.

text: What is the main purpose of a flat file database compared to a relational database?
optionA: It links tables using foreign keys
optionB: It stores all data in a single table with no relationships between tables
optionC: It uses SQL to query multiple tables simultaneously
optionD: It automatically backs up data to the cloud
explanation: A flat file database stores all data in one table; whereas a relational database uses linked tables to reduce redundancy.

text: A field that stores whether a student has paid their fees — either Yes or No — should use which data type?
explanation: A Boolean/Logical data type stores only two values (True/False or Yes/No); making it ideal for binary states.

text: Which of the following is an advantage of using a Database Management System (DBMS)?
optionA: Each department stores its own separate copy of the data
optionB: Data redundancy is increased to improve reliability
optionC: Multiple users can access the data simultaneously with consistent security
optionD: All data must be stored in a spreadsheet
explanation: A DBMS allows concurrent multi-user access; reduces redundancy; enforces security; and provides backup and recovery facilities.

text: A student creates a database form for entering new library records. What is the main purpose of this form?
optionA: To run complex queries on the data
optionB: To provide a user-friendly interface for entering and viewing records
optionD: To link tables via foreign keys
explanation: A data entry form provides a structured; user-friendly interface that makes it easier and less error-prone to enter records into a database.

text: A database query uses the criterion `> 50 AND < 100`. What data will this query return?
optionA: Records where the value equals 50 or 100
optionB: Records where the value is greater than 50 or less than 100
optionC: Records where the value is between 51 and 99 (exclusive)
optionD: Records where the value is exactly 75
explanation: The AND operator requires both conditions to be true; so only records where the value is greater than 50 AND less than 100 (i.e. 51–99) are returned.

text: In a database query; the wildcard symbol `*` is used to:
optionA: Search for a specific exact value
optionB: Match any sequence of characters in a field
explanation: The `*` wildcard matches any sequence of characters; allowing partial searches such as `Sm*` to find Smith; Smithson; etc.

text: What does the `<>` operator mean in a database query?
explanation: `<>` is the 'not equal to' operator; returning records where the field value does not match the specified criterion.

text: A table of products is to be sorted by price in ascending order; then by product name alphabetically within the same price. How many sort criteria are needed?
explanation: Two sort criteria are required: the primary key (price; ascending) and the secondary key (product name; alphabetically).

text: A field in a database links records in a 'Sales' table to records in a 'Customers' table. This linking field in the Sales table is called a:
explanation: A foreign key in one table references the primary key of another table; creating a relationship between the two tables.

text: Which of the following database operations would you use to find all students whose surname begins with the letter 'B'?
optionC: Apply a presence check on the surname field
optionD: Create a new table with just those records
explanation: The LIKE operator combined with a wildcard (`B*`) matches any value that begins with the letter B; allowing partial text searches.

text: A database report is designed to:
optionA: Allow users to enter new records
optionB: Display and summarise data in a formatted; printable layout
optionD: Create validation rules for data entry
explanation: A database report presents data from one or more tables in a formatted; often printable layout; suitable for sharing information with others.

text: A presentation slide is designed with a consistent logo; colour scheme; and footer on every slide using:
explanation: The master slide controls the consistent elements (logo; background; fonts; headers/footers) that appear on every slide in a presentation.

text: A teacher wants students to view a presentation automatically in a continuous loop at a school exhibition. Which output setting should be used?
explanation: A looped on-screen carousel allows the presentation to run automatically and continuously without any user interaction; ideal for exhibitions.

text: In a database report; a 'page footer' section appears:
optionA: Once at the very top of the report
optionB: At the bottom of every page
explanation: A page footer appears at the bottom of every page in a database report; typically showing page numbers or date/time.

text: Which of the following is the best description of an action button in a presentation?
optionA: A button that plays background music on all slides
optionB: A clickable object that navigates to a specified slide or opens an external file
optionC: An animated transition effect between slides
optionD: A button that prints the current slide
explanation: An action button is a clickable object in a presentation that can be configured to jump to another slide; open a file; or trigger other navigation actions.

text: A network that covers a single building or campus is best described as a:
explanation: A Local Area Network (LAN) covers a limited geographic area such as a building or campus; whereas a WAN covers large distances.

text: What is the primary function of a router in a network?
optionA: To increase the range of a Wi-Fi signal
optionB: To connect networks together and direct data packets between them
optionC: To convert analogue signals to digital
explanation: A router connects multiple networks (such as a home network to the Internet) and routes data packets to their correct destination.

text: A school wants to share its attendance database only with its own staff over a private internal network — not the Internet. This is best described as:
explanation: An intranet is a private internal network accessible only to authorised users within an organisation; not publicly accessible.

text: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are both wireless communication technologies. Which statement correctly compares them?
optionA: Bluetooth has a greater range than Wi-Fi
optionB: Wi-Fi is primarily used for connecting nearby peripheral devices such as headsets; whereas Bluetooth connects devices to the internet
optionC: Bluetooth is typically used for short-range device pairing; while Wi-Fi connects devices to a wider network over greater distances
optionD: Both Bluetooth and Wi-Fi operate at exactly the same frequency and power level
explanation: Bluetooth is designed for short-range connections (typically a few metres) between peripheral devices; while Wi-Fi provides network/internet access over a larger area.

text: A company allows selected external partners to access part of its private network. This is called:
explanation: An extranet is an extension of a company's intranet that provides controlled access to external users such as suppliers or partners.

text: In a network; a Network Interface Card (NIC) is used to:
optionA: Protect the network from external attacks
optionB: Physically connect a computer to a network
optionC: Increase the speed of the processor
explanation: A NIC (Network Interface Card) provides the hardware interface that allows a computer to connect to and communicate over a network.

text: Cloud computing allows users to store and access data over the Internet rather than on a local device. Which of the following is a key advantage of cloud storage?
optionA: It eliminates the need for any internet connection
optionB: Data can be accessed from any device with an internet connection
optionC: Files can only be opened on the device that created them
optionD: It is always faster than local storage
explanation: A major advantage of cloud storage is that data can be accessed from any location on any device with an internet connection.

text: What does URL stand for in the context of internet communication?
explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator — the web address used to locate a specific resource on the internet.

text: Which internet protocol is used to securely transfer web pages; encrypting data between the browser and the server?
explanation: HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure) encrypts the connection between a browser and a web server using SSL/TLS; protecting transmitted data.

text: A student evaluates a website and finds that the information was last updated three years ago. This raises concerns about which quality criterion?
explanation: Currency refers to how up to date the information is — older content may no longer be accurate; especially for rapidly changing topics.

text: FTP is primarily used for:
optionC: Transferring files between computers over a network
explanation: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is designed specifically for transferring files between computers or between a computer and a web server.

text: An Internet Service Provider (ISP) is a company that:
optionA: Manufactures network hardware such as routers and switches
optionB: Provides customers with access to the internet
explanation: An ISP (Internet Service Provider) is an organisation that provides individuals and businesses with access to the internet.

text: A user receives an email that appears to be from their bank; asking them to click a link and enter their login details. This is an example of:
explanation: Phishing involves fraudulent emails that appear to come from trusted sources; tricking users into revealing passwords or financial details.

text: A user receives a fraudulent text message on their mobile phone asking them to click a link to claim a prize. This attack is called:
explanation: Smishing is phishing carried out via SMS text messages on a mobile phone.

text: Which data protection method scrambles data so that it is unreadable without a decryption key?
explanation: Encryption converts data into an unreadable format using a key; ensuring that only authorised parties with the decryption key can read it.

text: A firewall is used to:
optionA: Remove viruses already on a device
optionB: Monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules
optionC: Encrypt files stored on a hard drive
optionD: Create secure backups of user data
explanation: A firewall acts as a barrier between a trusted internal network and untrusted external networks; filtering traffic according to predefined security rules.

text: Two-factor authentication (2FA) increases security by:
optionA: Requiring two separate passwords for every login
optionB: Using biometrics and passwords together as the only method
optionC: Requiring a second form of verification (such as a code sent to a phone) in addition to a password
optionD: Automatically logging users out after two minutes of inactivity
explanation: 2FA requires a second verification step (such as a one-time code sent by SMS) in addition to the standard password; reducing the risk of unauthorised access.

text: A data protection act requires organisations to follow principles when handling personal data. Which of the following is an example of personal data?
optionA: The number of products sold last year
optionB: A customer's name and home address
optionD: A list of publicly available company names
explanation: Personal data is information that can identify an individual; such as their name; address; date of birth; or medical history.

text: In HTML; which tag is used to define a row within a table?
explanation: `<tr>` (table row) defines a horizontal row within an HTML table; containing `<td>` (data) or `<th>` (header) cells.

text: A web developer adds the following CSS to their stylesheet: `h1 { color: blue; font-size: 24px; }`. Where should this external stylesheet be attached in the HTML document?
optionA: Inside the `<body>` tag at the bottom of the page
optionB: Inside the `<head>` section using a `<link>` tag
optionC: Inside every `<h1>` tag as an inline style
explanation: External CSS stylesheets are attached in the `<head>` section of an HTML document using a `<link rel="stylesheet" href="...">` tag.

text: In HTML; the `colspan` attribute is used to:
optionA: Merge a cell across multiple columns
optionB: Merge a cell across multiple rows
optionC: Set the width of a table column
optionD: Add a caption to a table
explanation: The `colspan` attribute specifies the number of columns a table cell should span; allowing cells to merge horizontally.

text: In web development; the three layers are content (HTML); presentation (CSS); and behaviour. Which technology forms the behaviour layer?
explanation: JavaScript forms the behaviour layer of a web page; controlling interactive and dynamic elements such as button clicks and animations.

text: A web developer uses an absolute file path for a hyperlink to a locally stored web page. Why is this considered bad practice?
optionA: Absolute paths are not recognised by web browsers
optionB: Absolute paths make the page load more slowly
optionC: If the files are moved to a different drive or computer; the absolute path will no longer work
optionD: Absolute paths cannot contain special characters
explanation: Absolute file paths reference a specific location on a specific device; so the link will break if files are moved to a different computer or folder. Relative paths are preferred for local resources.

text: Which HTML metatag attribute is used to make a web page display correctly on mobile devices?
explanation: The viewport metatag (`<meta name="viewport">`) controls how the browser scales the page on different devices; essential for responsive web design.

text: BCC (blind carbon copy) in an email is used to:
optionA: Send a copy of an email to the main recipient only
optionB: Send a copy of the email to additional recipients whose addresses are hidden from all other recipients
optionC: Reply to all recipients at once
optionD: Automatically forward an email to a mailing list
explanation: BCC sends a copy of the email to recipients whose addresses are not visible to any other recipients; useful for privacy when emailing a large group.

text: Copyright law as it applies to software means that:
optionA: Anyone can freely copy and distribute software once purchased
optionB: Software producers own the rights to their software and unauthorised copying is illegal
optionC: Software is free to use but cannot be modified
optionD: Only schools are allowed to copy software for educational use
explanation: Copyright law grants software producers exclusive rights over their product; making unauthorised copying (software piracy) illegal.

text: A student wants to share personal information — their home address — in a public social media post. Which advice should they follow?
optionA: Always share personal information to build a larger friend network
optionB: Avoid sharing personal data publicly as it could be misused by strangers
optionC: Share it only if the post is liked by more than 100 people
optionD: It is safe as long as the information is true
explanation: Personal data such as home addresses should never be shared publicly as it could be used for identity theft; stalking; or fraud.

text: Pharming involves:
optionA: Sending fraudulent SMS messages to mobile users
optionB: Redirecting users from a legitimate website to a fake one to steal login details
optionC: Installing a keylogger on a victim's computer
optionD: Calling victims by phone to obtain their bank details
explanation: Pharming redirects users to fraudulent websites even when they type the correct address; enabling attackers to harvest login credentials.

text: A satellite navigation system in a car uses GPS. Which characteristic best describes GPS?
optionA: GPS is a type of mobile phone network that provides voice calls
optionB: GPS uses a network of satellites to determine and display a device's geographic location
optionC: GPS is a protocol used to encrypt data sent over the internet
optionD: GPS is a type of LAN used in vehicles
explanation: GPS (Global Positioning System) uses a network of satellites to calculate the precise geographic location of a receiver; enabling navigation.

text: Vishing is a form of social engineering that involves:
optionB: Redirecting DNS requests to fake websites
optionC: Using voice calls to trick victims into revealing personal information
optionD: Installing malware through a USB drive
explanation: Vishing (voice phishing) uses telephone calls — often by fraudsters posing as banks or government agencies — to manipulate victims into providing sensitive information.

text: During the analysis phase of the systems life cycle; a systems analyst gathers information about the current system. Which method provides the most detailed insight into how users currently perform tasks?
explanation: Observation allows the analyst to see exactly how users interact with the current system in real time; revealing practical issues that may not emerge from questionnaires or document reviews.

text: A range check is an example of a validation routine. Which of the following data entries would a range check for values between 1 and 100 (inclusive) REJECT?
explanation: A range check accepts only values within the defined range (1–100 inclusive). The value 0 is outside this range and would be rejected.

text: During system testing; a developer uses data that falls exactly on the boundary of a valid range (e.g. exactly 0 or exactly 100 for a range of 0–100). This data is called:
explanation: Extreme (boundary) data tests the limits of valid input — values at the very edge of the accepted range — to ensure the system handles these cases correctly.

text: Which implementation method involves running the old system and the new system side by side until the new system is proven reliable?
explanation: Parallel running operates both the old and new systems simultaneously; allowing comparison of outputs and providing a fallback if the new system fails.

text: Technical documentation for a software system is primarily intended for:
optionA: End users who need to learn how to use the software
optionB: Programmers and engineers who need to maintain or modify the system
optionC: School management to decide on purchases
explanation: Technical documentation (including program listings; flowcharts; variable lists; and test data) is designed for developers and IT staff; not end users.

text: A new payroll system is introduced department by department over several months; rather than all at once. This is called:
explanation: Phased implementation introduces the new system gradually — section by section or module by module — reducing the impact of any problems that arise.
